producer_report.summary:
I fixed the false 'does not follow from the job's records' for an intervention re-score in a squash. `expected_score` in `crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs` now counts only interventions made at or before the score's own time. The full `cargo test --locked` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` runs pass. I ran `cargo fmt --all` but not `cargo fmt --check` afterwards.

Cause: a squash puts the closing score, the later intervention and its re-score in one tree. The old code recomputed the closing score from that whole tree, so it counted the intervention. That resolved the `user_intervenes` event to true early. The recorded score, made before the intervention, differs in that event's `outcome`, `provisional` and `brier`. A forged re-score still differs from `rescore()` of the correct closing score, so it is still refused.

Tests, in `landing_tests.rs`:
- A squash holding a landed job, an intervention and its re-score now passes. With the filter disabled it failed with 'events[2].brier.reader is 0.0225, but the records give 0.7224999999999999'.
- A squash with a forged re-score (all Brier values zeroed) is still refused with 'does not follow'.

I also added decision D71 to `docs/decisions.md` and a Fixed entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.

I did not run the real PR #9 squash, so I did not confirm the cause for jobs f1x7 and knqc. I reproduced it with the new test only.

I left `crates/athena-score/src/lib.rs` and `crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs` alone. The existing `hand_written_scores_and_outcomes_are_refused` test passes as is."

open_issues: I did not run the real PR #9 squash, so I did not confirm it for jobs f1x7 and knqc. The reproduction is the new test.
The time filter trusts the intervention's own `at`. A forged late `at` on an intervention is ignored for that score, but the re-score must still equal rescore() of the closing score.
Not changed, though listed as deliverables: crates/athena-score/src/lib.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs. The existing hand_written test passes as is.
mistakes: My first forged-rescore test used judge(), which never runs the score check, so it failed to detect forgery; I switched to also calling job_records_of.
learnings: A job has one score.json path; a re-score overwrites the closing score, so a squash holds only the latest score per job.
expected_score recomputed the closing score from the whole tree, so it counted interventions made after the closing score.
landing_tests.rs judge() runs invariant::check, not jobs::check; jobs::check needs job_records_of.
desires: The actual PR #9 squash, to confirm the two named jobs fail for this reason.
